name: Cycle Detection in Directed Dependency Graphs with Visited Array
description: In build systems (e.g. Webpack, Bazel) or task scheduling, circular dependencies (Task A -> Task B -> Task A) cause deadlocks. The engine must detect cycles and abort gracefully.
prompt:
In build systems (e.g. Webpack, Bazel) or task scheduling, circular dependencies (Task A -> Task B -> Task A) cause deadlocks. The engine must detect cycles and abort gracefully.

Execute the required analytical SQL calculation in DuckDB.
Expected output columns: task_id, depends_on, visited_path, has_cycle.
Row order does not matter.
setup_sql:
CREATE TABLE task_dependencies (
                task_id VARCHAR,
                depends_on VARCHAR
            );
            INSERT INTO task_dependencies VALUES
                ('compile', 'codegen'),
                ('codegen', 'lint'),
                ('lint', 'compile'); -- Circular cycle!
golden_sql:
-- Detect circular loops using array path tracking
            WITH RECURSIVE path_finder AS (
                SELECT 
                    task_id,
                    depends_on,
                    [task_id] AS visited_path,
                    false AS has_cycle
                FROM task_dependencies
                
                UNION ALL
                
                SELECT 
                    p.task_id,
                    d.depends_on,
                    list_append(p.visited_path, d.task_id),
                    list_contains(p.visited_path, d.depends_on) AS has_cycle
                FROM path_finder p
                JOIN task_dependencies d ON p.depends_on = d.task_id
                WHERE NOT p.has_cycle AND array_length(p.visited_path) < 10
            )
            SELECT 
                task_id,
                depends_on,
                visited_path,
                has_cycle
            FROM path_finder
            WHERE has_cycle = true
            LIMIT 1;
why_it_fails: Standard recursive CTEs without cycle tracking loop infinitely until the database crashes with out-of-memory errors.
